Earlier this year, when Apple launched the MacBook Neo, the personal computer market was clearly caught off guard. Although the aggressive pricing strategy of that laptop has been adjusted to suit market conditions, it took several months for Windows阵营 counterparts to announce their counterattack products one after another. Today it's HP's turn, releasing a new laptop equipped with an OLED screen, also starting from US$699—but there are quite a few conditions attached.

Overall, the HP OmniBook 5 14 looks like the MacBook Neo's body with an extra colourful budget version, paired with the more refined, understated green and blue colours of the Apple iPad Air series. Beneath its 14-inch screen, the body is just 11.77mm thick and weighs only 2.56 pounds—it could have perfectly caught the back-to-school shopping season, but HP just happened to miss this timing window. The real star of this machine is that 14-inch display—at this price point, you'd normally only see IPS panels, but this time there are two OLED options for you to choose from, which I'll discuss in detail later. The two sides of the body feature two 'full-function' USB-C ports and a headphone jack, and when you open the screen, an FHD camera supporting Windows Hello is immediately ready.

In terms of hardware specifications, HP says this laptop supports up to an Intel Core 7 processor, but the model on display only showed this one configuration. Battery life looks quite impressive on the spec sheet—up to 42 hours of local video playback (battery capacity unspecified)—though admittedly, local video playback tests may not fully reflect real-world usage. HP mentioned this machine is compatible with their 65W mini GaN charger, which is expected to be included with the machine. Beyond that, known specs also include dual microphones and 'Poly Studio-tuned' audio; if you feel there's still a lot of information missing, then you are definitely not alone.

Firstly, the processor model for the US$700 version of this laptop remains a mystery, making it difficult to directly compare with Apple's A18 Pro. HP has also chosen not to disclose any information about storage or memory configurations—not even wording like 'up to'—which precisely reflects the considerable pressure the PC market is under given the current tight memory supply. Even the most noteworthy selling point comes with a rather fatal trade-off: HP spent a great deal of time at the launch event describing that 2.5K OLED display, but that version won't ship until March 2027. The model going on sale later this month at Best Buy comes with a 2K OLED display, but the brightness drops drastically from 650 nits to just 300 nits.

Given so many missing details, and some answers that are disappointing, if HP has still managed to pique your interest, stay tuned for more information to be released before the product officially goes on sale.
